item.title: Correction · Channel Pump Station: The Channel Pump Station record said it was built in 1979…
item.description: The Channel Pump Station record said it was built in 1979, upgraded in 2010, rated 103 million gallons per day and the largest of five combined-sewer pump stations, citing the DataSF Assessor roll and an SF Chronicle article. Neither states any of that, and the article is about Stormwater Pump Station #6, a different building. The record now cites SF Planning's Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, chapter 7, which gives 455 Berry St, constructed 1979, upgraded 2010, 103 mgd, and continuous dry and wet weather operation. The 'largest of five' claim and the sentence about a round, tiled design were removed because no source read supports them for this station. The 1979 milestone now cites the same report. Source: SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 Wastewater, 2020 (https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/default/files/plans-and-programs/planning-for-the-city/sea-level-rise/SLRVCA_Report_07.pdf); San Francisco Chronicle, John King, 2015-10-26 (https://www.sfchronicle.com/bayarea/article/A-Mission-Bay-pump-station-delivers-chic-design-6587800.php) (does not state this); DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls, parcel 3806006 (https://data.sf.gov/resource/wv5m-vpq2.json?parcel_number=3806006) (does not state this).
